input.reasoning: I searched ten framings before deciding: the claim as written, the proposed canonical form, a plain paraphrase, the direct negation ("the probability... increases as collision energy increases"), the contrary ("more likely at lower energies"), a cross-section/technical paraphrase, a baryon-number mechanism wording, a heavy-ion wording, an accelerator-comparison wording, and the broader strangelet-danger framing. Every search returned the same small neighbor cluster, with no result matching this proposition under any wording or its negation. The nearest candidates all fail the identical-decomposition test: "Collisions at the LHC present no danger" is a broad safety verdict turning on many independent considerations (black holes, monopoles, vacuum stability, whether stable strangelets exist, cosmic-ray bounds), so evidence bearing on an energy-dependence correlation bears on it only partially. The cosmic-ray-in-dense-stars and cosmic-ray-equivalent claims are parallel safety arguments about different mechanisms, and the microscopic-black-holes claim concerns a different hypothetical object altogether. The candidate is a single empirical correlation about how strangelet production probability varies with collision energy, plausible as an extracted premise (its verbatim emphasis on "decreases" reads as a corrective assertion within the LHC-safety debate). No existing node holds it, so per the recoverable-error principle I create it rather than force a match onto the broader safety claim. The proposed canonical form is terse, frame-independent, and affirmative; I adopt it as given.
input.direction_note: Stated as the affirmative form of the energy-dependence question the discourse argues: "decreases as energy increases" positively asserts the correlation's direction rather than negating its opposite, and a source holding either view of the trend would accept the form as a fair statement of what is in dispute.

It is a generalization counterpart of the two cosmic-ray claims (8df4a5b0..., ea8dd956-8fc0-4780-94c1-541ac1f71345): those argue from cosmic-ray experience that LHC hazards are excluded, while this one states the within-collision energy dependence that motivates part of that reasoning; neither entails the other.
